title: Schiller CARDIOVIT AT Series Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Battery Not Charging
description: EKG not charging, running only on battery, or shutting down due to power source, battery, or connection issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the device is in use, transfer the patient to another EKG machine before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify Wall Outlet Power
steps.instructions: Plug in another device to confirm power. Try a different outlet if needed.

steps.title: Inspect AC Power Cord and Adapter
steps.instructions: Ensure connections are fully seated at both ends. Look for frayed wires, bent prongs, or loose connectors. Swap with a known good cord/adapter if available.

steps.title: Confirm AC Power Indicator on Device
steps.instructions: Plug in the device and observe indicator lights. Power the unit on if possible.

steps.title: Check Battery Charging Status on Display
steps.instructions: Look for charging symbol or percentage increase. Note any battery-related warnings or messages.

steps.title: Perform a Power Reset
steps.instructions: Power off the unit. Disconnect AC power. Wait 30–60 seconds. Reconnect power and restart.

steps.title: Check for Docking Station or External Charger (If Applicable)
steps.instructions: Ensure the device is properly seated. Inspect docking contacts for dirt or damage. Try a different dock if available.

steps.title: Inspect for Environmental or Physical Issues
steps.instructions: Check for excessive heat near battery area. Look for liquid exposure or corrosion.

CCR.Complaint: EKG machine not charging and shutting down during use.
CCR.Cause: Battery failed to accept charge after verifying power cord, outlet, and adapter were functional.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service and sent to Clinical Engineering for battery replacement and evaluation.

title: Schiller CARDIOVIT AT Series Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Touchscreen or Keypad Not Responding
description: Troubleshooting unresponsive touchscreen or keypad issues on Schiller CARDIOVIT AT Series EKG machines.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the device is in use, stop acquisition and move the patient to another functioning EKG machine.

steps.title: Verify Device Power and Screen Activity
steps.instructions: Confirm power LED indicators are on, look for screen backlight or faint image, and attempt to power the unit off and back on.

steps.title: Perform a Full Reboot
steps.instructions: Shut down the device completely, disconnect AC power for 30 seconds, then reconnect and power back on.

steps.title: Inspect Touchscreen Surface or Keypad Condition
steps.instructions: Ensure screen is clean and dry, remove gloves or moisture, and inspect keypad for stuck or damaged buttons.

steps.title: Check for Screen Lock or Software Mode Restrictions
steps.instructions: Look for lock icons, attempt alternate controls, and verify the interface is not frozen.

steps.title: Test External Input (if applicable)
steps.instructions: Connect a compatible external keyboard or input device if supported.

steps.title: Inspect for Signs of Physical Damage or Liquid Intrusion
steps.instructions: Check for cracks, residue, fluid exposure, or unusual behavior like ghost touches.

CCR.Complaint: EKG touchscreen not responding to input during patient setup.
CCR.Cause: Touchscreen unresponsive after reboot; no external damage noted.
CCR.Resolution: Removed from service and sent for evaluation of touchscreen interface.

helpfulDetails: Signs of physical damage or contamination

title: Schiller CARDIOVIT AT Series Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Lead Fail or Poor Signal Quality
description: Troubleshooting lead fail messages and poor ECG signal quality caused by electrodes, cables, or connections.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the ECG is being used for diagnosis, ensure the patient is stable and move to another functioning EKG machine if needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to acquire an ECG and observe waveform, checking for lead fail alerts, no signal vs noisy signal, and baseline wander or artifact.

steps.title: Inspect Electrode Placement and Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm proper placement, replace dried or loose electrodes, and clean the skin to ensure good contact.

steps.title: Check Lead Wire Connections (Patient Cable)
steps.instructions: Ensure all leads are firmly connected, inspect for damage or corrosion, and reattach any loose connections.

steps.title: Inspect and Swap Patient Cable (Lead Set)
steps.instructions: Check for cable damage, manipulate cable while observing waveform, and swap with a known good cable if available.

steps.title: Check Trunk Cable Connection to the Unit
steps.instructions: Ensure the connector is fully seated, inspect for bent pins or debris, and reseat the cable.

steps.title: Minimize Electrical Interference
steps.instructions: Move cables away from power sources, prevent patient contact with metal surfaces, and reduce nearby electrical devices.

steps.title: Check Filter and Gain Settings
steps.instructions: Verify correct filter settings and adjust gain to ensure a clear and readable waveform.

steps.title: Perform System Reset (If Needed)
steps.instructions: Power cycle the unit, reconnect cables, and attempt ECG acquisition again.

CCR.Complaint: EKG showing lead fail and poor waveform quality during acquisition.
CCR.Cause: Worn patient cable with intermittent internal break causing signal loss.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced patient lead cable and verified proper signal acquisition on all leads.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (returned to service or removed)

title: Schiller CARDIOVIT AT Series Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Thermal Printer Failure or Paper Feed Errors
description: Troubleshooting printer not feeding paper, paper jams, blank prints, or poor print quality on Schiller CARDIOVIT AT Series EKG machines.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the device is in use, stop ECG acquisition and move the patient to another EKG machine if printing is required. Expected: Patient care continues without interruption. Why it matters: Printing issues should not delay diagnosis or documentation.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to print a test ECG or stored report. Observe: No paper feed, paper stops mid-print, blank or faded output, error messages on display. Expected: Issue is reproducible and clearly identified. Why it matters: Confirms whether this is a feed issue, jam, or print quality problem.

steps.title: Check Paper Supply and Type
steps.instructions: Open the printer compartment and inspect the paper roll. Ensure paper is present and not empty. Confirm correct thermal paper type for Schiller AT Series. Check that paper width matches device requirements. Expected: Proper paper is installed. Why it matters: Incorrect or missing paper is a common cause of feed and print issues.

steps.title: Verify Paper Orientation
steps.instructions: Confirm the thermal paper is loaded correctly. Ensure paper feeds from the correct direction (thermal side aligned with print head). Reload paper if unsure. Expected: Paper feeds smoothly when printing. Why it matters: Incorrect orientation results in blank prints or no output.

steps.title: Inspect for Paper Jam or Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check inside the printer compartment. Remove any jammed or torn paper. Ensure no debris is blocking the feed path. Gently clear obstructions without forcing components. Expected: Paper path is clear and unobstructed. Why it matters: Even small obstructions can prevent proper feeding.

steps.title: Check Printer Cover and Latch
steps.instructions: Ensure the printer door is fully closed and latched. Open and firmly close the printer cover. Listen/feel for proper latch engagement. Expected: Printer recognizes the cover as closed and allows printing. Why it matters: Many units will not print if the cover is not properly secured.

steps.title: Perform a Test Feed or Calibration
steps.instructions: Use the device’s feed or test print function. Press paper feed button (if available). Run internal test print if accessible. Expected: Paper advances smoothly and prints clearly. Why it matters: Helps isolate feed mechanism vs system issue.

steps.title: Inspect Print Quality (If Feeding Occurs)
steps.instructions: If paper feeds but print is poor: Look for faded, uneven, or missing print. Clean print head using approved method (lint-free cloth if accessible). Replace paper roll with a new one. Expected: Clear, legible ECG printout. Why it matters: Dirty print heads or degraded paper affect output quality.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Restart the EKG machine. Turn off the unit. Wait 10–15 seconds. Power back on and retry printing. Expected: Printer resets and functions normally. Why it matters: Clears minor system or printer communication faults.

CCR.Complaint: EKG machine not printing; paper not feeding during ECG acquisition.
CCR.Cause: Paper roll installed incorrectly, preventing proper feed.
CCR.Resolution: Reinstalled paper correctly and verified proper feed and print function.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or error messages observed
Indicator lights or printer status messages

title: Schiller CARDIOVIT AT Series Electrocardiograph (EKG) Machine - Network or EMR Connectivity Failure
description: Troubleshooting guide for ECG devices not transmitting data to EMR due to network or configuration issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not delay ECG acquisition due to connectivity issues. If needed, print or store the ECG locally.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Confirm ECG saves locally but does not export, check for error messages, and determine if failure is intermittent or complete.

steps.title: Check Physical Network Connection (Wired Systems)
steps.instructions: Ensure Ethernet cable is seated, check link lights, swap cable, and test different wall port.

steps.title: Verify Wi-Fi Connection (If Applicable)
steps.instructions: Confirm Wi-Fi enabled, check signal strength, reconnect to correct SSID.

steps.title: Confirm Network Configuration Settings
steps.instructions: Verify valid IP address, subnet, gateway, and DHCP/static configuration.

steps.title: Check EMR / Server Configuration Settings
steps.instructions: Verify server IP/hostname, port, protocol, department assignment, and device ID.

steps.title: Attempt Test Transmission
steps.instructions: Send a test ECG and observe for errors, success, or delays.

steps.title: Check for Network-Wide Issues
steps.instructions: Determine if other devices are affected and involve IT if necessary.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Restart the device to clear temporary communication faults.

CCR.Complaint: EKG not transmitting studies to EMR; staff reports export failures.
CCR.Cause: Misconfigured network settings with incorrect gateway address.
CCR.Resolution: Corrected network configuration and verified successful test transmission.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (working or removed from service)

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Battery Will Not Charge, Is Not Detected, or Has Short Runtime
description: Troubleshoots battery detection, charging, and runtime problems involving seating, contacts, charging source, battery condition, or power-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Emergency Defibrillator Availability
steps.instructions: If battery condition is questionable, place another verified defibrillator into service before troubleshooting. A defibrillator with unreliable battery operation should not be assigned to transport or emergency response. Expected outcome: Patient care and emergency response remain protected.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Battery Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the battery: Is not detected. Does not charge. Charges only intermittently. Appears charged but discharges rapidly. Causes shutdown when AC is removed. Produces an unexpected battery warning. Record the displayed status. Expected outcome: The battery problem is clearly reproduced or characterized.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC and Charging Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit or charging bracket is receiving reliable AC power. Inspect: Power cord. External supply, if applicable. Outlet operation. Charging indication. Expected outcome: A valid charging source is present. If restoring AC power resolves the problem, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Remove and Reinstall the Battery
steps.instructions: With the unit safely removed from patient use, remove and reinstall the battery according to normal approved handling practices. Check that it seats and latches correctly. Expected outcome: The battery is securely installed and recognized.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Battery and Device Contacts
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible battery contacts and mating surfaces for: Dirt. Bent contacts. Corrosion. Foreign material. Cracks. Swelling or physical damage. Do not use a battery showing physical damage or abnormal heat. Expected outcome: Contacts are clean and undamaged and the battery is physically safe for testing.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Battery
steps.instructions: Install an approved known-good compatible battery. Observe whether the device detects and charges it normally. Expected outcome: A known-good battery operates normally. If the original battery alone fails, remove the original battery from service and replace it according to facility policy.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate Short Runtime
steps.instructions: If the battery is detected and charges but runtime is poor, fully charge it using approved procedures and perform the applicable battery-performance evaluation. Do not assume a runtime problem based only on an estimated display value. Expected outcome: Battery performance meets the applicable manufacturer or facility requirement. If not, replace the battery.

steps.title: 8. Check Operation During AC Removal
steps.instructions: Using an approved nonclinical test setup, verify that the defibrillator remains operational when external power is removed. Expected outcome: The unit transfers to battery operation without unexpected shutdown or reset.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm battery detection, charging indication, battery operation, and return to charging when external power is restored. Expected outcome: Battery and charging behavior are stable and repeatable. If so, return the unit to service according to policy.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the DEFIGARD Touch 7 shut down shortly after being disconnected from AC power.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the installed battery had substantially reduced usable runtime while a known-good battery operated normally.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the battery and verified charging, AC-to-battery operation, and acceptable battery performance before returning the unit to service.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Charging Bracket Will Not Charge the Battery or Detect the Device
description: Troubleshoots charging-bracket problems involving AC power, device seating, contacts, cabling, battery condition, or the bracket itself.

steps.title: 1. Protect Emergency Readiness
steps.instructions: If the unit cannot maintain a dependable battery charge, ensure another verified defibrillator is immediately available before removing this unit from service. Do not rely on a questionable charging system for emergency equipment readiness. Expected outcome: Clinical coverage is maintained while the charging problem is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The bracket has no power indication. The device is not detected when docked. Charging starts and stops. The battery percentage does not increase. The unit charges through another approved method but not the bracket. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as a bracket, connection, device, or battery-related symptom.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power to the Bracket
steps.instructions: Confirm the charging bracket is connected securely to its intended power source. Check: Power cord seating. External power supply connections, if applicable. Outlet operation using an approved outlet tester or known-good equipment. Visible damage to the cord or plug. Expected outcome: The bracket receives reliable AC power. If restoring the power connection resolves charging, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Device Seating and Alignment
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the DEFIGARD Touch 7 in the charging bracket. Confirm the unit is fully seated and not being held out of position by: Straps. Cables. Debris. Cart hardware. Bent or damaged mounting components. Expected outcome: The device seats completely and consistently in the bracket. If proper seating restores detection and charging, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Charging Contacts and Connectors
steps.instructions: With power removed as appropriate, inspect accessible charging contacts and mating surfaces for: Dirt. Oxidation. Bent contacts. Foreign material. Physical damage. Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: Charging contacts are clean, aligned, and undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Check the Defibrillator and Battery
steps.instructions: Confirm the battery is correctly installed and recognized by the defibrillator. If an approved known-good compatible battery is available, substitute it to determine whether the symptom follows the battery. Expected outcome: A known-good battery is detected and charges normally. If the original battery alone fails, remove that battery from service.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Charging Bracket
steps.instructions: When available, place the unit in another compatible, verified charging bracket. Alternatively, test another verified compatible DEFIGARD Touch 7 in the suspect bracket. Expected outcome: The comparison isolates the problem to the defibrillator, battery, bracket, or installation.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Charging Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting any external issue, confirm that the device is detected consistently when docked and that the charging indication remains stable. Verify that battery charge status progresses appropriately according to approved testing practices. Expected outcome: The device remains detected and charging is stable. If so, document the result and return the equipment to service.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the DEFIGARD Touch 7 did not begin charging when placed in its charging bracket.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the defibrillator was not seating fully because an accessory cable was trapped behind the unit.
CCR.Resolution: Repositioned the accessory cable, fully seated the defibrillator in the bracket, and verified stable device detection and battery charging.

helpfulDetails: Battery status before and after docking.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - ECG Has Persistent Artifact, Lead-Off, or Incorrect Heart Rate
description: Troubleshoots ECG problems involving electrodes, lead wires, patient cable, placement, interference, configuration, or ECG input faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Monitoring
steps.instructions: If ECG monitoring is unreliable and the patient requires continuous rhythm surveillance, move monitoring to another verified device or provide an approved alternate monitoring method. Do not troubleshoot unreliable ECG monitoring while it is the patient's only required rhythm-monitoring source. Expected outcome: Reliable patient monitoring continues during evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the ECG Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported problem is: Persistent artifact. Lead-off indication. No waveform. Incorrect heart rate. One lead affected. All leads affected. Intermittent dropout. Compare the displayed ECG with the clinical situation before assuming an equipment fault. Expected outcome: The exact ECG failure is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect and Replace Electrodes
steps.instructions: Check for: Dry electrodes. Expired electrodes. Poor adhesion. Excessive hair. Moisture. Improper skin preparation. Incorrect placement. Replace electrodes and prepare the skin according to clinical practice. Expected outcome: Electrodes maintain reliable skin contact and the waveform stabilizes. If the issue resolves, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Lead Wires and ECG Cable
steps.instructions: Check the patient cable and lead wires for: Loose connections. Damaged insulation. Bent contacts. Contamination. Strain damage. Intermittent connections near cable ends. Reconnect each lead securely. Expected outcome: All ECG connections are intact and lead-off indications clear.

steps.title: 5. Substitute Known-Good ECG Accessories
steps.instructions: Use an approved known-good ECG patient cable or lead-wire set when available. Expected outcome: If the known-good accessory restores normal ECG operation, remove the failed accessory from service.

steps.title: 6. Check for External Electrical or Motion Artifact
steps.instructions: Determine whether artifact changes when: The patient stops moving. Nearby powered equipment is disconnected or moved. Lead wires are separated from power cords. The unit operates on battery rather than AC, when safe and appropriate. Do not disconnect clinically necessary equipment from a patient simply for troubleshooting. Expected outcome: External interference is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 7. Verify ECG Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm appropriate user-accessible settings such as lead selection and any normal filtering or monitoring configuration relevant to the clinical workflow. Do not alter protected configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: ECG settings are appropriate for the intended monitoring application.

steps.title: 8. Test With an Approved Patient Simulator
steps.instructions: Remove the defibrillator from clinical use and connect an approved ECG simulator. Verify waveform appearance, lead detection, and heart-rate response. Expected outcome: The DEFIGARD Touch 7 displays a stable simulated ECG and correct corresponding heart rate. If so, the device is functioning normally and troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Reconnect the normal accessory set or verified replacement accessories and confirm stable ECG monitoring. Expected outcome: ECG waveform, lead status, and heart rate remain reliable.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported persistent ECG artifact and intermittent lead-off indications on the DEFIGARD Touch 7.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an intermittent connection in the ECG lead-wire set while the monitor displayed a stable waveform with a known-good cable.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the ECG lead-wire set and verified stable waveforms, lead detection, and heart-rate accuracy using an approved simulator.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Integrated Printer Feeds but Produces a Blank or Distorted Trace
description: Troubleshoots printer output problems involving paper installation, paper type, contamination, door closure, feed path, or the print mechanism.

steps.title: 1. Preserve Clinical Documentation
steps.instructions: If printed records are required and the integrated printer is unreliable, preserve ECG and event information using another approved documentation method. Do not delay patient care solely to troubleshoot the printer. Expected outcome: Required clinical information remains available while the printer is evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Printer Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the printer: Feeds blank paper. Produces a faint trace. Produces a distorted or compressed trace. Prints intermittently. Skews or wrinkles the paper. Produces normal text but poor waveforms. Expected outcome: The exact print-quality problem is reproduced.

steps.title: 3. Verify Correct Paper Installation
steps.instructions: Open the printer compartment and verify that the paper is: Installed in the correct orientation. Loaded through the proper feed path. Not folded or jammed. Not excessively loose or tightly compressed in the compartment. Expected outcome: Paper feeds smoothly and is oriented correctly. If proper loading restores printing, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Approved Paper
steps.instructions: Confirm that the paper is the correct approved type for the printer. Thermal paper installed backward or inappropriate paper can feed normally while producing a blank output. Expected outcome: Correct compatible paper is installed. If replacing the paper restores the trace, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Paper and Feed Path
steps.instructions: Check for: Damp or damaged paper. Adhesive residue. Torn paper. Debris. Misaligned roll or stack. Obstruction in the feed path. Remove accessible debris without disassembling the printer mechanism. Expected outcome: The paper path is clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Inspect and Clean Accessible Print Surfaces
steps.instructions: With the device removed from clinical use and following approved procedures, inspect accessible print-head and roller surfaces for contamination. Clean only using methods approved for the equipment. Expected outcome: Accessible print surfaces are clean and free of residue.

steps.title: 7. Check Printer Door Closure
steps.instructions: Verify that the printer door closes fully and maintains proper paper contact. Inspect hinges, latches, and visible alignment for damage. Expected outcome: The printer door closes securely and paper remains properly aligned.

steps.title: 8. Produce a Controlled Test Print
steps.instructions: Print an approved test strip or recorded waveform. Compare the printed trace to the displayed waveform. Expected outcome: The paper advances evenly and produces a clear, undistorted trace. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the DEFIGARD Touch 7 printer fed paper normally but produced blank strips.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the thermal paper had been installed with the printable surface facing the wrong direction.
CCR.Resolution: Reloaded the approved paper correctly and verified clear ECG traces and normal paper feeding on repeated test prints.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Manual/AED Shock Will Not Arm, Charge, or Discharge
description: Troubleshoots shock-delivery failures involving mode selection, pads, therapy cables, controls, battery power, connections, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Immediately
steps.instructions: If shock delivery is required or may become necessary and the DEFIGARD Touch 7 cannot reliably arm, charge, or discharge, immediately place another verified defibrillator into service. Do not continue troubleshooting a therapy-delivery fault while a patient depends on the affected unit. Expected outcome: Emergency defibrillation capability is maintained using reliable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the unit: Will not enter the required therapy mode. Will not recognize the connected therapy accessory. Will not begin charging. Charges but will not arm for shock. Arms but will not discharge. Displays an unexpected therapy-related message. Record the exact displayed message if present. Expected outcome: The failure stage is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Basic Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit starts normally and has adequate available power for testing. Connect approved external power when applicable and verify the installed battery is detected. If power behavior is abnormal, resolve the power issue before continuing. Expected outcome: The defibrillator has stable power and is ready for controlled bench testing.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Therapy Pads, Paddles, and Cable Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect the therapy accessory and cable for: Incomplete insertion. Bent or damaged contacts. Damaged insulation. Contamination. Expired or compromised disposable pads. Incorrect accessory connection. Reconnect all components fully. Expected outcome: The proper therapy accessory is connected securely and is recognized by the device.

steps.title: 5. Substitute Known-Good Therapy Accessories
steps.instructions: When permitted, use approved known-good therapy pads, paddles, or therapy cable to determine whether the problem follows the accessory. Do not perform uncontrolled shock testing. Expected outcome: A known-good accessory is recognized and allows the therapy sequence to proceed normally. If the original accessory causes the failure, remove it from service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Mode and Control Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended Manual or AED operating mode is selected using normal user-accessible controls. Verify that charge, arm, and shock controls respond normally during an approved test sequence. Do not enter restricted service modes. Expected outcome: Controls respond predictably and the unit advances through the expected therapy sequence.

steps.title: 7. Test With an Approved Defibrillator Analyzer
steps.instructions: Remove the unit from clinical use and connect an approved defibrillator analyzer according to facility and manufacturer procedures. Perform the applicable functional shock-delivery test without connecting the device to a patient. Expected outcome: The device charges and discharges appropriately into the analyzer and passes required functional verification. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify Both Applicable Therapy Workflows
steps.instructions: If the unit supports both Manual and AED operation in the local configuration, verify the previously reported mode and any additional mode required by facility return-to-service procedures. Expected outcome: Therapy operation is reliable and repeatable with no unexpected interruption.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the DEFIGARD Touch 7 would not charge for defibrillation when therapy pads were connected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the therapy cable was not fully seated and the pads were therefore not being recognized.
CCR.Resolution: Fully connected the therapy cable and verified successful charging and shock delivery into an approved defibrillator analyzer.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - NIBP, SpO2, or CO2 Parameter Module Will Not Acquire a Reading
description: Troubleshoots parameter failures involving sensors, cuffs, tubing, sampling accessories, patient connection, module detection, settings, or external accessory faults.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Required Patient Monitoring
steps.instructions: If NIBP, SpO2, or CO2 monitoring is clinically required and the DEFIGARD Touch 7 cannot obtain a dependable reading, provide the parameter using another verified monitor before troubleshooting. Do not rely on intermittent or unreliable parameter data. Expected outcome: Required monitoring remains available throughout evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Affected Parameter
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: NIBP. SpO2. CO2. Multiple parameters simultaneously. Record any displayed message and whether the parameter is detected but not producing a value. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to one monitoring path or identified as a broader device problem.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Patient Accessory
steps.instructions: For the affected parameter, inspect the external accessory: NIBP Cuff condition. Correct tubing connection. Kinks. Leaks. Damaged connectors. SpO2 Sensor condition. Cable connection. Contamination. Damaged optical surfaces. Excessive ambient light or motion. CO2 Sampling line. Airway adapter. Water trap or moisture-management accessory, when present. Kinks or blockages. Loose connections. Expected outcome: The accessory path is intact and correctly connected.

steps.title: 4. Replace Disposable or Easily Substituted Accessories
steps.instructions: Use an approved known-good cuff and hose, SpO2 sensor, or CO2 sampling accessory as applicable. Change one component at a time when practical. Expected outcome: If the reading returns with a known-good accessory, remove the failed accessory from service and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify Module or Parameter Detection
steps.instructions: Confirm the parameter is shown as available by the DEFIGARD Touch 7 and that no obvious module-disconnected or sensor-disconnected condition remains. Reconnect any approved external module or accessory connection that is intended to be user-removable. Expected outcome: The parameter is recognized and ready to acquire data.

steps.title: 6. Check Patient and Environmental Factors
steps.instructions: When troubleshooting a clinical report, consider external causes such as: Patient motion. Poor perfusion affecting SpO2. Incorrect cuff placement or size selection. Loose CO2 sampling connection. Condensation or secretion blockage. External light interference. Use a simulator or analyzer for technical verification rather than relying solely on a patient comparison. Expected outcome: Patient-dependent factors are separated from equipment performance.

steps.title: 7. Verify User-Accessible Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm that normal parameter settings and monitoring modes have not unintentionally disabled the measurement or prevented acquisition. Do not change protected configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The parameter is enabled and configured appropriately for testing.

steps.title: 8. Test With Approved Simulation Equipment
steps.instructions: Remove the unit from clinical use and use appropriate approved test equipment for the affected parameter, such as: NIBP simulator/analyzer. SpO2 simulator when compatible with the installed technology. CO2 simulator or gas source approved for the test method. Expected outcome: The parameter acquires and displays a stable test value according to the applicable verification procedure.

steps.title: 9. Compare With Known-Good Accessories or Configuration
steps.instructions: If available, compare the suspect parameter using known-good accessories from another verified compatible system. Avoid changing protected hardware configuration solely for troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to the accessory or remains with the DEFIGARD Touch 7.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Repeat the measurement several times as appropriate for the parameter and confirm stable acquisition without disconnect or error indications. Expected outcome: The affected parameter produces repeatable, reliable readings. If so, document the correction and return the device to service.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the DEFIGARD Touch 7 SpO2 parameter detected the sensor but would not display a saturation reading.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the SpO2 sensor produced no reading on the device while a known-good compatible sensor operated normally.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective SpO2 sensor and verified stable parameter acquisition and display during functional testing.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Pads, Paddles, or Therapy Cable Is Not Recognized
description: Troubleshoots therapy-accessory recognition problems involving pads, paddles, connectors, cables, accessory condition, or the device therapy interface.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Immediate Defibrillation Capability
steps.instructions: If the therapy accessory is not recognized while a patient may require defibrillation, immediately use another verified defibrillator. Do not continue troubleshooting a therapy-accessory fault while the patient depends on the affected device. Expected outcome: Reliable defibrillation capability remains available.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Accessory Is Not Recognized
steps.instructions: Identify whether the issue involves: Adhesive therapy pads. External paddles. Therapy cable. One particular accessory set. All therapy accessories. Record any displayed message. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to a specific accessory path or shown to affect all therapy connections.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Therapy Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect and inspect the therapy connector for: Incomplete insertion. Bent or damaged contacts. Debris. Fluid contamination. Loose connector housing. Cable strain damage. Reconnect it firmly. Expected outcome: The therapy cable seats securely and the device recognizes the accessory.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Pads or Paddles
steps.instructions: Check pads or paddles for: Physical damage. Contamination. Expired or compromised disposable packaging. Damaged connectors. Broken or loose cable attachment. Do not use damaged or compromised therapy accessories. Expected outcome: The accessory is appropriate and physically intact.

steps.title: 5. Substitute Known-Good Therapy Accessories
steps.instructions: Use approved known-good pads, paddles, or therapy cable as applicable. Change one component at a time when possible to isolate the failed item. Expected outcome: The known-good accessory is recognized. If the failure follows the original accessory, remove that accessory from service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Normal Therapy Mode Detection
steps.instructions: Using an approved bench setup, verify that connecting the intended therapy accessory produces the expected normal device response. Do not perform uncontrolled therapy discharge. Expected outcome: The unit consistently detects the connected therapy accessory.

steps.title: 7. Test Therapy Function With an Analyzer
steps.instructions: Connect the defibrillator to an approved defibrillator analyzer using the verified accessory path and perform applicable functional testing. Expected outcome: The accessory remains recognized and therapy operation completes successfully. If so, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the DEFIGARD Touch 7 displayed that the connected therapy pads were not recognized.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an intermittent therapy cable connection and confirmed normal recognition with a known-good cable.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the therapy cable and verified reliable pad detection and therapy operation using an approved defibrillator analyzer.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Touchscreen Is Unresponsive or Miscalibrated While Wearing Gloves
description: Troubleshoots touchscreen response problems involving gloves, contamination, protective films, positioning, external damage, or a persistent touch-interface fault.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Defibrillation Capability
steps.instructions: If the DEFIGARD Touch 7 is connected to or supporting a patient and touchscreen control is unreliable, transfer monitoring and emergency-response readiness to another verified defibrillator before troubleshooting. Do not continue using a defibrillator whose controls cannot be operated predictably. Expected outcome: Patient care continues on reliable equipment and the affected unit is available for safe evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Touchscreen Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the screen: Does not respond anywhere. Responds only in certain areas. Selects an adjacent control. Requires excessive pressure. Works with bare fingers but not while wearing gloves. Responds intermittently. Restart the unit only when it is not being relied upon for patient care and observe whether normal touch operation returns. Expected outcome: The failure is reproduced consistently or is shown to have been temporary. If normal operation returns and remains reliable through functional testing, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Screen Surface
steps.instructions: Check the display for: Moisture. Gel. Cleaning residue. Blood or other contamination. Cracked glass. Deep scratches. Impact damage. A loose or lifting protective film. Clean and dry the display using approved facility and manufacturer-compatible methods. Expected outcome: The screen is clean, dry, undamaged, and free of anything that could interfere with touch detection. If cleaning restores reliable operation, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Compare Gloved and Ungloved Operation
steps.instructions: Using clean hands and appropriate gloves, compare touchscreen response without gloves and with the glove type normally used by clinical staff. Do not change clinical glove requirements simply to make the device usable. Expected outcome: The touchscreen responds reliably during normal intended operation. If the problem occurs only with a specific glove type, document the finding and verify whether an approved operating method or configuration applies before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 5. Check for External Screen Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect for unauthorized screen protectors, overlays, adhesive labels, transport covers, or other materials contacting the touchscreen. Remove only accessories that are clearly nonessential and approved for removal. Expected outcome: Nothing external is interfering with the touchscreen. If removing an inappropriate overlay restores normal response, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 6. Check Control Behavior Across the Display
steps.instructions: With the device removed from clinical use, test several normal touchscreen selections across different areas of the screen. Also verify any available physical controls required for operation. Do not enter restricted service or calibration menus unless authorized by manufacturer documentation. Expected outcome: Touch locations correspond correctly with displayed controls and respond consistently. Persistent offset, dead areas, or unintended selections indicate the unit should remain out of service.

steps.title: 7. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem occurs only when the screen is wet, heavily contaminated, extremely cold or warm, or immediately after cleaning. Allow the unit to return to normal operating conditions before retesting. Expected outcome: Touch performance remains reliable under normal clinical conditions.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify normal startup and accessible operational controls according to approved procedures. Confirm that touch selections are repeatable and do not activate unintended functions. Expected outcome: The touchscreen responds accurately and consistently. If so, document the correction and return the device to service according to facility policy.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the DEFIGARD Touch 7 touchscreen responded inconsistently while they were wearing gloves.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found cleaning residue on the touchscreen surface that caused inconsistent touch response during gloved operation.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned and dried the touchscreen, verified accurate response with normal clinical gloves across the display, and completed functional testing successfully.

helpfulDetails: Whether the problem affects the entire screen or specific areas.
Glove type used when the issue occurs.
Whether a restart changed the condition.
Results of touch testing across the screen.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Transcutaneous Pacing Has No Capture or Output Is Out of Tolerance
description: Troubleshoots pacing problems involving pad contact, cable recognition, ECG sensing, user settings, patient factors, or pacing-output verification.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Pacing Capability
steps.instructions: If transcutaneous pacing is clinically required and the DEFIGARD Touch 7 is not producing effective therapy, immediately provide another verified pacing-capable device or alternate treatment as directed by the clinical team. Do not troubleshoot uncertain pacing output while the patient depends on the unit. Expected outcome: Required pacing support continues using reliable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Distinguish No Capture From No Pacing Output
steps.instructions: Clinical noncapture does not automatically indicate equipment failure. Determine whether the device: Does not enter pacing mode. Does not recognize therapy pads. Shows pacing markers but no clinical capture. Produces no apparent pacing output. Fails output verification on test equipment. Expected outcome: The symptom is separated into a device-output problem, accessory problem, or patient-capture concern.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Therapy Pads and Placement
steps.instructions: For a patient-related report, clinical staff should verify pad condition and placement according to their approved clinical procedure. For bench troubleshooting, inspect pads, adapters, and therapy cables for damage and secure connection. Expected outcome: Approved therapy accessories are correctly connected and recognized.

steps.title: 4. Substitute Known-Good Therapy Accessories
steps.instructions: Use approved known-good pads and therapy cables for bench evaluation. Expected outcome: The device recognizes the replacement accessory and pacing behavior becomes stable if the original accessory was defective.

steps.title: 5. Verify ECG Signal Quality
steps.instructions: Demand pacing depends on reliable ECG sensing. Check for: Lead-off conditions. Excessive ECG artifact. Poor electrode contact. Unstable heart-rate detection. Use an approved simulator during bench testing. Expected outcome: The device receives a stable ECG signal suitable for pacing evaluation.

steps.title: 6. Verify User-Accessible Pacing Controls
steps.instructions: Confirm that the appropriate pacing mode, rate, and output controls respond normally during an approved bench test. Do not use service-level calibration adjustments unless authorized. Expected outcome: Pacing controls respond predictably and the device generates pacing indications as expected.

steps.title: 7. Verify Output With an Approved Analyzer
steps.instructions: Connect the defibrillator to an approved defibrillator/pacer analyzer using the manufacturer-appropriate test setup. Measure pacing output according to approved manufacturer and facility procedures. Expected outcome: Pacing output meets the applicable specified requirement. If output passes, the device fault is not reproduced and troubleshooting can stop after documenting the result.

steps.title: 8. Verify Demand/Fixed Pacing Behavior as Applicable
steps.instructions: Using a simulator and analyzer, verify the pacing mode involved in the original complaint and any additional pacing functions required by the return-to-service procedure. Expected outcome: Pacing output and sensing behavior are reliable and repeatable.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that transcutaneous pacing from the DEFIGARD Touch 7 did not appear to produce capture.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering verified normal pacing output on an approved analyzer and found that the equipment fault could not be reproduced with known-good therapy accessories.
CCR.Resolution: Completed pacing and ECG functional verification, documented normal device output, and returned the unit to service after successful testing.

title: Schiller DEFIGARD Touch 7 Defibrillator - Wi-Fi, Cellular, ePCR, or SentioWeb Data Transfer Fails
description: Troubleshoots data-transfer failures involving network availability, wireless signal, configuration, destination systems, credentials, or infrastructure.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Care and Documentation
steps.instructions: Do not delay emergency treatment because electronic data transfer is unavailable. Ensure patient information, ECG records, and treatment documentation are preserved using an approved alternate workflow while troubleshooting occurs. Expected outcome: Patient care and required clinical documentation continue without dependence on the failed data connection.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Transfer Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects: Wi-Fi connection. Cellular connection. ePCR transfer. SentioWeb communication. One case only. All cases. One destination or all destinations. Record any displayed network or transfer message. Expected outcome: The affected communication path is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the Device Is Otherwise Operating Normally
steps.instructions: Verify the DEFIGARD Touch 7 starts normally and that patient monitoring and therapy functions are not affected. If the device exhibits broader instability, remove it from service rather than treating the problem as communications-only. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to connectivity or data transfer.

steps.title: 4. Check Wireless Signal and Environment
steps.instructions: Move the device, when clinically appropriate, to an area where reliable facility Wi-Fi or cellular service is normally available. Check for: Poor coverage. Shielded rooms. Basements. Elevators. Temporary network outages. Known cellular dead zones. Expected outcome: The device has adequate wireless coverage. If transfer succeeds in a known-good coverage area, document an environmental or infrastructure-related issue.

steps.title: 5. Verify User-Accessible Network Status
steps.instructions: Review normal status indications for Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity without altering protected network settings. Confirm whether the device is: Connected. Searching. Disconnected. Connected locally but unable to reach the destination. Expected outcome: Network status is clearly established.

steps.title: 6. Compare With Another Device or Location
steps.instructions: Determine whether another configured DEFIGARD Touch 7 or compatible hospital device can communicate from the same location. If multiple devices fail simultaneously, involve the appropriate network, cellular, ePCR, or application support team. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the individual device or identified as an infrastructure/service issue.

steps.title: 7. Check Data Workflow and Destination Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm that the intended ePCR or SentioWeb destination is available and that the reported record has been finalized or made ready for transfer according to local workflow. Do not alter protected credentials or destination configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The data is in a transferable state and the intended receiving service is available.

steps.title: 8. Retry With a Test or Approved Nonclinical Record
steps.instructions: When permitted by policy, perform a controlled data-transfer test using an approved test record or workflow. Expected outcome: Data reaches the intended destination successfully. If transfer is restored and repeatable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the device reconnects normally after restart or movement between expected coverage areas, if applicable, and that no clinically required records remain unsent. Expected outcome: Communication is stable and expected data is transferred or otherwise accounted for.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that treatment records from the DEFIGARD Touch 7 were not transferring to the ePCR system over Wi-Fi.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the unit was being used in an area with inadequate wireless coverage while identical devices transferred normally elsewhere.
CCR.Resolution: Verified successful transfer from a known-good coverage area and referred the location-specific wireless issue to the appropriate network support team.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or all records fail.
